newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says it begins deploying Patriot missiles.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says it begins deploying Patriot missiles.

text.p: Taiwan has started deploying an initial batch of newly arrived U.S. Patriot missile systems, saying it needs the weapons to counter possible attacks from China, the defence minister said.

"The (initial) batch of Patriot missile systems have arrived, and assembly work is going smoothly. After completion and practices, we will display them to the public," Chiang Chung-ling told the state-funded Central News Agency over the weekend.
"In the face of missile threats by the Chinese communists, it is absolutely a must for us to deploy Patriot missiles for self-defence," Chiang said.
Taiwan has ordered 200 sets of Patriot missiles and launchers from the United States.
Chiang said China currently has deployed a Russian SA300 anti-missile system in its southern province of Guangdong.
China staged a series of war games off Taiwan between August 1995 and March 1996 to try to intimidate the island for what it saw as a growing independence trend in Taiwan.
China has said it would retake the island should it officially break from the mainland.
He said there is a need for Taiwan to buy more foreign weapons to defend itself against military threats from China.
